form.label: mispfetch
form.description: MISP custom command mispfetch to retrieve events or attributes or events with their attributes (Streaming command) - check https://github.com/remg427/misp42splunk/ for any update

search.query: | rest /services/configs/conf-misp42splunk_instances | rename eai:acl.app as app, title as misp_instance | fields misp_instance

html.p: The command mispfetch is a streaming command. It cannot be on a first line of a SPL (this is a key difference with mispgetioc and mispgetevent).
It can take parameters from the command line or from the result set before. The values coming from the result set have priority over the values passed on the command line.
This way is very flexible to adapt the REST HTTP body of the request against one of the 2 supported MISP REST API endpoints: /events/restSearch or /attributes/restSearch
It has only one mandatory parameter "misp_instance:" that has to be set when the command is invoked. The following SPL are equivalent:

tr.td: One of the accounts defined in tab configuration (the list is also displayed on the drop-down list if your account has the permissions to use the command rest - if not, simmly type the name of the account in the input field next to the drop-down list)
Use this parameter to select between the endpoint "/events/restSearch" or "/attributes/restSearch".

td.p: if misp_http_body is not provided, it is set to
Provide an HTTP body in JSON format.
You can test it using the MISP RESP graphical client on MISP.
you can also use a SPL to prepare it.
⚠️ 2 keys are enforced on any HTTP body

Limit the number of attributes per event when fetching events and getioc is True (in that case, the param limit applies to the number of events). This parameter has no effect when fetching attributes (use limit in that case).
Effective only when using /events/restSearch.
Boolean to have object attributes expanded (one per row). By default, attributes of one object are displayed on the same row.
Effective when fetching attributes.
Include event attributes in the output. In tabular view there will be one row per object or attribute of events.
When False, the request sets metadata=1 so MISP returns event metadata only. Measured on a 1900-event search that is roughly 33 KB per event, against several MB per event with getioc=True.
Effective only when using /events/restSearch.
Keep the Galaxy clusters attached to each event.

When False, the request sets excludeGalaxy=1 so MISP never builds them. This is the single largest saving available: galaxy clusters arrive with their full definitions and measured around 400 KB per event.
It can also be useful for misp_output_mode=json if you plan to use spath, which has a default limit of 5000 characters to parse the JSON payload.
Effective only when using /events/restSearch.
Keep the RelatedEvent list attached to each event.

When False the request asks for includeEventCorrelations=0, but MISP 2.5.33 ignores that filter, so RelatedEvent is still transferred and then discarded. Check the [MC-807] line in search.log for how much that costs on your instance.
Effective only when using /events/restSearch.

tr.td: Define the limit for each MISP search; default 1000. 0 = no pagination
Results are displayed using the native Splunk tabular view or JSON events
Comma(,)-separated string of tags to exclude. Wildcard is %.

td.p: Sort order sent to MISP, as "Model.field [asc|desc]" rules separated by commas. MISP applies no ORDER BY unless asked, and paging an unordered query with limit/page can return overlapping or missing rows between pages, so a stable sort is what makes a multi-page fetch correct.

Ordering by event_id first also lets results stream page by page, so memory follows limit rather than the size of the whole result set. Change the first key and the whole result set is buffered instead.

MISP 2.5 accepts only: Attribute.id, Attribute.event_id, Attribute.object_id, Attribute.type, Attribute.category, Attribute.value, Attribute.distribution, Attribute.timestamp, Attribute.object_relation and Event.publish_timestamp. Set order=none to send no sort order.
Effective only when using /attributes/restSearch; the events endpoint has different sortable fields.

tr.td: define the page for each MISP search; default 0 = iterate through all pages. With limit=0 the page number is dropped from the request.

split combined attribute types such as domain|ip
Effective when fetching attributes.

prefix set to every MISP key. The value is set in order by
this parameter, then by the value defined for the instance in the configuration pane and finally default to "misp_"
Comma(,)-separated string of tags to search for. Wildcard is %.

html.p: Three settings in the app Configuration tab bound a search. Each one reports at ERROR in search.log when it stops a run, so a partial result is never silent:

ul.li: Max Response Size (MB) bounds what is transferred from MISP, reported as [MC-803] for events and [MC-603] for attributes.
Max Execution Time (seconds) bounds how long the fetch may run, reported the same way.

Max Output Size (MB) bounds what is handed to Splunk, reported as [MC-808]. Splunk buffers every result in memory until the command finishes, so this is what stops a very wide search from hanging with no output.

html.p: Two other lines are worth knowing. [MC-802] gives the number of events fetched alongside MISP's own X-Result-Count, which is the quickest way to tell a complete answer from a truncated one. [GR-004] counts values that exceeded Splunk's 2 MB field limit and had to be cut; if you see it, try expand_object=True so each attribute becomes its own row instead of being merged into one oversized row.

Both paths stream a page at a time, so memory follows limit rather than the size of the whole result set. On the attributes path this requires an order starting with Attribute.event_id, which is the default: attributes of one event then arrive together, and a group split across a page boundary can be held back and completed from the next page. Override order with something else and the whole set has to be held in memory instead.

The same information reaches the results: every row carries a <prefix>mispfetch_message field (by default misp_mispfetch_message) with the matched total and the reason the fetch stopped, if it did. Results are streamed, so the last rows carry the most complete message. Each row also carries <prefix>mispfetch_params, the resolved parameter set used for that request.
Setting a limit to 0 disables it. Leaving all of them at 0 is not recommended, since nothing then bounds a runaway search.
The misp_http_body parameter accepts a JSON string that is sent as the HTTP body to the MISP REST API.
The easiest is with the command | tojson <list_of_fields> output_field=misp_http_body
Below are working examples you can copy and paste. Adjust to the misp instances you have defined
Example 1: Fetch events published in the last 7 days

pre.code: | makeresults | eval last="7d", published="true" | tojson last, published output_field=misp_http_body | mispfetch misp_instance=misp

html.p: Example 2: Fetch attributes with event metadata and tags

pre.code: | makeresults | eval last="30d", includeEventUuid=1, includeEventTags="true" | tojson last, includeEventUuid, includeEventTags output_field=misp_http_body | mispfetch misp_instance=misp

html.p: Example 3: Fetch events by specific event IDs and change the prefix

pre.code: | makeresults | eval eventid=mvappend("12345", "12346", "916b86b0-2e1e-452e-8691-1fddf970e2ba") | tojson eventid output_field=misp_http_body | mispfetch misp_instance=mispdev prefix=mispdev_

html.p: Example 4: Fetch attributes filtered by type and category

pre.code: | makeresults | eval last="14d", type=mvappend("ip-dst", "domain", "hostname"), category="Network activity" | tojson category last type output_field=misp_http_body | mispfetch misp_instance=misp misp_restsearch=attributes

| makeresults | eval misp_instance="mispdev", misp_prefix="mispdev_", misp_restsearch="attributes" | eval last="14d", type=mvappend("ip-dst", "domain"), category="Network activity", enforceWarninglist=1 | tojson category last type enforceWarninglist output_field=misp_http_body | mispfetch

ul.li: Boolean values in JSON should be lowercase (or use 0 & 1): true or false
The following keys are enforced/overridden: returnFormat=json, withAttachments=false
You can use the tags and not_tags command parameters instead of including them in misp_http_body
